THE GLOBAL EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS PUSH CONTINUES — CANADA, THAILAND, MOLDOVA & THE EUROPEAN UNION!

Many have been tracking the growing number of governments encouraging citizens to stockpile emergency supplies in preparation for potential cyberattacks, blackouts, infrastructure failures and other major disruptions.

The announcements keep coming.

FOUR MORE DEVELOPMENTS IN THE LAST SEVERAL DAYS:

🇨🇦 CANADA — NOVEMBER 11

Insider Paper highlights renewed attention to Canada’s recommendation that citizens maintain at least 72 HOURS of emergency supplies in case of power outages, cyberattacks or disruptions to essential services.

The guidance itself isn’t new, but the renewed attention certainly fits the broader preparedness narrative we’ve been tracking.

🇹🇭 THAILAND — NOVEMBER 2–9

Authorities urge households to prepare 72-HOUR EMERGENCY SURVIVAL BAGS, citing potential cyberattacks, sabotage, international conflict and critical infrastructure disruptions.

🇲🇩 MOLDOVA — NOVEMBER 9–10

Government announces its FIRST NATIONAL EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS CAMPAIGN, scheduled for November 19–21.

The initiative includes emergency backpacks, public warning systems and crisis-response exercises.

🇪🇺 EUROPEAN UNION — NOVEMBER 3

The European Commission presents new household preparedness guidance emphasizing 72 HOURS OF SELF-SUFFICIENCY across its 27 member states.

We’ve already documented new emergency stockpiling guidance across at least 13 COUNTRIES, alongside escalating cybersecurity warnings, attacks on emergency-alert systems, disruptions to European food refrigeration infrastructure and major power outages.

And now we’re seeing additional governments and international organizations expanding or renewing their public preparedness messaging.

WHY ARE SO MANY GOVERNMENTS NOW EMPHASIZING A 72-HOUR WINDOW?

The 72-hour recommendation is a longstanding emergency-management standard, but the renewed attention across multiple countries is worth examining.

Are we witnessing a broader international effort to improve civilian resilience, or is there something more driving this sudden concentration of preparedness messaging?

Sources: Insider Paper, Public Safety Canada, European Commission, Thailand disaster authorities and Moldova government announcements — November 2026.
